title: What Scripture Actually Means by "Delight Yourself in the Lord"
caption:
Guys quote Psalm 37:4 like an equation. Delight in God long enough, hard enough, and he hands you a wife on schedule.

That's not faith. That's a vending machine with God's name taped to it.

The verse was never describing a delivery. It's describing a changed man. Delight isn't the payment you make, it's the practice that reshapes what you actually want. Spend enough real time with him and your list stops being yours. It starts looking like his.

And a wife was never the finish line. If she's the reason you're chasing God, you're not pursuing him, you're using him. A walk with God that ends at a ring was never a walk with God. It was a strategy with a verse taped to it.

Delight is what you do this morning. The Word open before the group chat. A prayer with nothing riding on it, said because he's worth talking to, not because he owes you an answer.

That ache isn't shaped for a wife. It's shaped for God, and he fills it first.

theme: He chases God, not a wife.
